title: Promotion follows retained scope references
takeaway: The scheduler reads the promoted scope when it selects pending work; active requests continue.
assumptions: All components and connections describe current code. Positions are schematic. The client path applies when the shared operation uses this client; the supplied source does not show a direct inflight join caller.

entities.label: Interactive caller
entities.summary: Caller context supplies the priority used by joinGitHubWork.

entities.label: Shared GitHub read
entities.summary: Owns GitHubWork and joins it before registering each shared reader.

entities.label: Client request work
entities.summary: Runs request attempts under a child scope and handles paced results outside scheduler slots.

entities.label: Scheduler
entities.summary: Retains task scopes and selects pending interactive tasks before lower priorities. It does not enforce rate limits.

entities.label: Active requests
entities.summary: Started tasks continue until completion. Exclusive work blocks new starts; permitted parallel work can use up to three active slots.

relationships.label: Join existing work
relationships.summary: The wrapper joins before shared.read; a higher caller priority raises the existing work scope.

relationships.label: Retain parent scope
relationships.summary: When the operation creates client work, createGitHubWork retains the current scope as its parent; effective priority follows that chain.

relationships.label: Submit request attempt
relationships.summary: The client supplies its current scope and permits parallel execution only for read-only work with parallel reads enabled.

relationships.label: Return paced result
relationships.summary: A paced result sends control back to the client loop, which sleeps before another submission.

relationships.label: Start when permitted
relationships.summary: Selection does not bypass exclusivity or capacity. Parallel starts require task permission and effective interactive priority.

plan.question: How can an interactive caller promote existing work without replacing it or interrupting an active request?
plan.visualApproach: Use a fixed responsibility map. Put the shared work scope above the child client scope, then place scheduler selection below both. Place active requests across a separate start boundary.
plan.whyThisForm: The important relationship is scope ownership and retained references, not movement through a numeric queue. The map separates promotion from permission to start.
plan.encodings: Boxes identify responsibilities. Downward connections show scope inheritance and submission. The side connection shows a join. The final boundary separates pending selection from active requests. All entities are context.
plan.motion: Use one static frame. Scope references and the start boundary explain the rule without implying a specific execution trace or interruption.
plan.prediction: If a parent work scope becomes interactive while a child task is pending, the next scheduler selection can see interactive priority, but an active exclusive request still blocks its start.
plan.restingState: The caller join, parent reference, retained task scope, retry path, and active-request boundary remain visible.

scenarios.title: Existing work keeps its identity
scenarios.input: An interactive caller joins shared work whose operation uses the GitHub client.

frames.title: Scope promotion reaches pending selection
frames.caption: The join changes shared scope state. The scheduler reads effective priority later; it does not interrupt active requests.
